cues.zh: 而且该市还取消了最低停车位要求
cues.en: And the city has removed minimum parking requirements
for 2 downtown neighbourhoods,

cues.zh: 试图打造一个更适宜步行的
cues.en: in an attempt to build a more walkable
mixed-use downtown.
Speaking of mixed-use,

cues.zh: 一个常见误解是休斯顿没有区划。
cues.en: it is a common myth that Houston does not have zoning.

cues.zh: 没错，这座城市并没有一种叫“区划”的东西，
cues.en: It’s true that the city does not have a thing called 'zoning',
but they have lots of other restrictions,
such as minimum parking requirements,
minimum lot sizes,

cues.zh: 以及其他城市通常会写进区划法规的规定。
cues.en: and other regulations that cities would normally put into their zoning codes.

cues.zh: 而且还有市政府强制执行的
cues.en: And they also have city-enforced
deed restrictions that limit

cues.zh: 你在某些地块上能建什么，
cues.en: what you can build on certain parcels of land,
that allows, for example,

cues.zh: 许多社区只建独栋住宅。
cues.en: only single-family homes to be built in many neighbourhoods.
In short,

cues.zh: 休斯顿把所有分区条例中最糟糕的部分都占了，
cues.en: Houston has all of the worst parts of a zoning ordinance,
they just don’t call it 'zoning'.

cues.zh: City Beautiful 有一个很棒的视频讲这个
cues.en: City Beautiful has a great video about this
if you’re interested in learning more.

cues.zh: 但尽管已经做了这么多工作，
cues.en: But despite all the work that is being done,
Houston has a very, very,
very long way to go.

cues.zh: 这座城市最近完成了一个耗资数百万美元的项目
cues.en: The city recently completed a multimillion-dollar project

cues.zh: 被称为“行人保护交叉口”。
cues.en: that is called a “protected intersection for pedestrians".

cues.zh: 你觉得这看起来对行人友好吗？
cues.en: Does this look pedestrian-friendly to you?

cues.zh: 这是两条六车道“街道-公路混合体”的交叉口，
cues.en: It is the intersection of two 6-lane stroads,

cues.zh: 而且它真的有供司机使用的高速滑行车道，
cues.en: and it literally has high-speed slip lanes for drivers

cues.zh: 让他们右转时绕过红绿灯。
cues.en: so that they can bypass the traffic light when turning right.

cues.zh: 滑行车道对行人来说极其危险。
cues.en: Slip lanes are insanely dangerous for people walking.
It’s absolutely ridiculous

cues.zh: 工程师竟然故意设计滑行车道
cues.en: that engineers would purposefully design slip lanes

cues.zh: 在一个本应是为行人准备的地方，
cues.en: in a place that’s supposedly meant for pedestrians,
and being billed as "pedestrian-friendly".
I mean, I guess it’s better

cues.zh: 穿过草地、走过没有便道的“死亡之桥”要好吧？
cues.en: than walking through the grass and across a death-bridge with no sidewalk?
But come on!
This is what counts as "pedestrian infrastructure"?
And of course,
Houston is also home to the Katy freeway,

cues.zh: 它是美国最宽的高速公路。
cues.en: the widest freeway in the United States.
2.2 billion dollars was spent

cues.zh: 把这条高速拓宽到20多条车道，
cues.en: widening the highway to over 20 lanes,
and as a result,

cues.zh: 从市中心出发的通勤时间反而增加了
cues.en: travel times out of downtown have increased
by up to 30%.
This is a massive sum of money

cues.zh: 本可以更好地用于公共交通
cues.en: that could have been better spent on public transit

cues.zh: 或其他替代开车的方案，
cues.en: or other alternatives to driving

cues.zh: 这些方案已被证明能减少汽车交通，
cues.en: that are proven to reduce car traffic,

cues.zh: 但它却被用来做了一场昂贵的示范，
cues.en: but instead it was used as an expensive demonstration
of induced demand.

cues.zh: 而且这里没有吸取任何教训。
cues.en: And no lessons have been learned here.
The city and state are planning an additional
7 billion dollars on highway expansion.
This project will demolish
4 religious buildings,
2 schools,
168 homes,
1,067 multifamily units,
and 331 businesses

cues.zh: 这些企业雇用了近 25,000 人。
cues.en: that employ almost 25,000 people.
It is literally
never-ending.
It’s often said that
the truth about a city’s aspirations
isn’t found in its vision,
it’s found in its budget.

cues.zh: 所以，尽管花了数百万改善步行设施
cues.en: So despite the millions spent on pedestrian improvements

cues.zh: 却还莫名其妙地包含让司机更快转弯的车道，
cues.en: that somehow also include faster turning lanes for drivers,

cues.zh: 休斯顿仍在汽车基础设施上投入数十亿，
cues.en: Houston is spending billions on car infrastructure,

cues.zh: 并且完全沉迷于汽车依赖。
cues.en: and is fully addicted to car-dependency.

cues.zh: 我只是……不知道该怎么消除这些损害
cues.en: I just... don’t know how you undo the damage

cues.zh: 它们是由这样一个地方的设计造成的。
cues.en: caused by a place designed like this.

cues.zh: 这到底怎么可能变得可持续？
cues.en: How does this ever become sustainable?
Financially or environmentally?

cues.zh: 而对我来说，最可悲的部分
cues.en: And to me, the most sad part

cues.zh: 是那些从小到大只知道汽车依赖的人
cues.en: is that people who have grown up only knowing car dependence
don’t see a problem with this.
To them, restricting cars is

cues.zh: 就是在剥夺他们的自由，
cues.en: literally taking away their freedom,

cues.zh: 因为他们已经对汽车依赖上瘾，
cues.en: because they have become so addicted to car-dependency
that they are incapable of understanding

cues.zh: 其实可以设计出这样的地方：
cues.en: that it is possible to design places where,

cues.zh: 在那里你不仅不需要开车，
cues.en: not only do you not need to drive,
you won’t even want to drive,

cues.zh: 而且这种生活方式可以更好，
cues.en: and that lifestyle can be better

cues.zh: 几乎在方方面面都更好。
cues.en: in almost every way.

cues.zh: 我的旅行让我有机会走访
cues.en: My travels gave me the opportunity to visit
every major city in the United States,

cues.zh: 其中大多数还去过多次。
cues.en: most of them multiple times.
And as a result,
I have absolutely no desire
to go back to any of them.

cues.zh: 但这些经历塑造了我对城市的看法，
cues.en: But those experiences shaped the way I think about cities,

cues.zh: 也正是它们最终促使我们一家
cues.en: and they're what ultimately resulted in our family
moving to the Netherlands,

cues.zh: 这个拥有世界上最好城市的国家。
cues.en: the country that has the best cities in the world.
And hey,

cues.zh: 如果休斯敦没那么糟糕，
cues.en: if Houston weren’t so terrible,

cues.zh: 我们也就不会有这个 YouTube 频道了，所以……
cues.en: we never would have this YouTube channel, so...
thanks, Houston!
I owe you one.

cues.zh: 我要感谢我在 Patreon 上的支持者们，
cues.en: I’d like to thank my supporters on Patreon,

cues.zh: 他们花钱让我重温那些糟糕的旧时光。
cues.en: who pay me to relive the bad ol’ days.

cues.zh: 如果你想支持这个频道，
cues.en: If you’d like to support the channel,

cues.zh: 并获得额外视频的观看权限，
cues.en: and get access to bonus videos,
visit Patreon.com/notjustbikes.
